reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker directs viewers to sign up through their referral link and purchase a HashFlare contract in exchange for a stated five-percent cryptocurrency return. The separate Litecoin giveaway is described as a future, undecided reward, and the Internxt claims are presented in a service review.

citations.quote: a small... Token review of the Internext ERC-20 token, which I belive is quite interesting
I bought in at a point three dollars
I believe that this token will go really far and do great stuff
you seriously seriously check this out

opening.argument: The presentation is explicitly qualified as personal opinion rather than a promise. The speaker says he “personally believe[s]” the token can be significant, tells viewers “it’s up to you,” and describes the proposed Litecoin amount as undecided. The description also identifies the video as “not sponsored in any way.” Those qualifications matter: viewers are given uncertainty, personal perspective, and a stated absence of sponsorship, not a guaranteed investment result or a concealed endorsement.

citations.quote: which I personally believe can truly be the big token
But its up to you, i am just telling you, this is out there
I'm not decided if i should do a 5 dollar or a 10 dollar giveaway
(THIS VIDEO IS NOT SPONSORED IN ANY WAY)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The referral wording does mention a purchase and a five-percent amount, but it also explains that the amount depends on what the speaker earns. That is a conditional referral arrangement, not a guaranteed investment return. The separate giveaway is expressly undecided, so the opening’s characterization of a solicitation should not transform every qualified statement into a promise.

citations.quote: i will send five percent for what i earned back to you
I'm not decided if i should do a 5 dollar or a 10 dollar giveaway

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not remove the promotional substance. The speaker still asks viewers to use his HashFlare link and purchase a stated amount of hashing power, then describes sending five percent back. Personal-opinion language and an undecided giveaway do not address the token appreciation pitch or the purchase-linked benefit.

citations.quote: if you use my Hashflare link to sign up, and you purchase, let say, 1 TeraHash
i will send five percent for what i earned back to you
I believe that this token will go really far and do great stuff

opening.argument: The video's stated format is news commentary and a token review. The speaker introduces “some news flowing around in the crypto-space,” identifies the segment as a “Token review,” walks through Internxt’s stated service model, and points viewers to the white paper for a more technical overview. The material therefore supports an interpretation centered on explaining a cryptocurrency project and discussing market developments, with the speaker repeatedly marking conclusions as his own opinion.

citations.quote: I'm going to talk about some news flowing around in the crypto-space
a small... Token review of the Internext ERC-20 token
I believe we have not even seen half of its potential, not even a tenth
Whitepaper: https://internxt.io/whitepaper.pdf

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a review does not make the favorable investment messaging disappear. The speaker reports his own purchase, says the token can go far, and tells viewers to check it out. Those are not merely neutral explanations of technology or market news; they connect the discussion to a token’s prospective value.

citations.quote: I bought in at a point three dollars
I believe that this token will go really far and do great stuff
you seriously seriously check this out

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The review framing is not neutral when it repeatedly promotes future potential. The speaker says he bought the token, claims its potential has barely been seen, and directs viewers to check it out. Discussing a white paper or reading a project website does not establish that the content is only educational rather than encouraging acquisition.

citations.quote: I bought in at a point three dollars
I believe we have not even seen half of its potential, not even a tenth
you seriously seriously check this out

opening.argument: The HashFlare portion is presented as an ordinary referral promotion with a disclosed benefit, not as a hidden investment mechanism. The speaker says viewers should use his link, explains that he receives value from a qualifying purchase, and describes returning five percent of what he earns. The description labels the offer as cashback and separately calls the Litecoin item a giveaway. The supplied material does not show a guaranteed profit, a downline-income promise, or a request for credentials; it describes a service referral and a conditional promotional benefit.

citations.quote: Get 5% cashback when purchasing a contract on HashFlare
if you use my Hashflare link to sign up, and you purchase, let say, 1 TeraHash
what i will do is to take um i will get value in bitcoin
i will send five percent for what i earned back to you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The offer is not merely an ordinary discount: it requires signing up through the speaker’s link and purchasing a contract, while the speaker receives value from that purchase. The stated five-percent return is tied to his earnings, but that condition still makes the purchase-linked benefit part of the promotion.

citations.quote: if you use my Hashflare link to sign up, and you purchase, let say, 1 TeraHash
I will get 100 GB hasheshes because that's ten percent
i will send five percent for what i earned back to you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Labeling the arrangement cashback does not make it harmless commerce. The speaker solicits a qualifying purchase through his referral link and receives a benefit based on that purchase, while offering a return calculated from his earnings. The absence of a guaranteed profit or credential request does not negate the purchase-linked solicitation.
